Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (4) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Survey tests can expose project credentials 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>briefs/survey.md tells the survey subagent to install repository-declared dependencies and run the
>repository's test command without first isolating that execution from its credentials. When an
>existing project's checkout contains a malicious install hook or test script, that code runs in the
>architect's cloud environment, which can contain project secrets and authenticated GitHub access.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[briefs/survey.md[16]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9/files#diff-d3c8eaeb6fa550717fd87047d4342e84343884d10239787568920657a6d794e8R16-R16) > >```diff >+2. Find the test command. Run it once from the checkout. You may install the dependencies the repo itself declares. Stop after about 10 minutes, and record why it didn't finish. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The architect clones the existing repository and gives that checkout to the survey subagent. The
>brief permits dependency installation and test execution; its prohibitions on printing secrets do
>not constrain code executed by package hooks or tests. The architect protocol also describes project
>secrets in the cloud environment.
>
> > [ARCHITECT.md\[130-138\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/ARCHITECT.md/#L130-L138) > [briefs/survey.md\[15-28\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/briefs/survey.md/#L15-L28) > [ARCHITECT.md\[214-218\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/ARCHITECT.md/#L214-L218) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The survey runs repository-controlled install hooks and tests in an environment that may hold project credentials. >## Fix Focus Areas >- briefs/survey.md[15-28] >- ARCHITECT.md[130-138] >## Recommended Fix >Require the architect to run survey installs and tests in a disposable environment without GitHub authentication or project secrets, with restricted network access. Have the survey report tests as unverified when that isolation is unavailable. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/bef7ab1b-cc5b-40f1-a954-1bca80fe6811?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/bef7ab1b-cc5b-40f1-a954-1bca80fe6811)

2. Help can delay replacing a silent lead 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The changed lease take --takeover help says a replacement may start once the architect finds the
>old lead gone, but the unchanged join-line --takeover help still requires LEAD-SILENT. When a
>lead dies while waiting for the owner, the watchdog stays quiet, so an architect following the
>conflicting join-line help may wait for an alarm that will not come.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[1603]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R1603-R1603) > >```diff >+ help="take it even from another session: only for a lead Matthew starts once the architect finds the old lead gone") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The PR changes one takeover help string while the sibling join-line help retains the former
>restriction. The new architect protocol explicitly permits takeover of an unresponsive lead waiting
>for the owner and says the watchdog remains quiet in that state.
>
> > [room.py\[1600-1603\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/room.py/#L1600-L1603) > [room.py\[3353-3356\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/room.py/#L3353-L3356) > [ARCHITECT.md\[365-373\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/ARCHITECT.md/#L365-L373) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The two takeover help messages give conflicting conditions for replacing a lead that is waiting for the owner. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[1600-1603] >- room.py[3353-3356] >## Recommended Fix >Update the `join-line --takeover` help to match the new lease-taking rule, including the case where the architect confirms a waiting lead is gone without a LEAD-SILENT alarm. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/e0e41f88-994a-4892-b8ca-b0c903d5484c?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/e0e41f88-994a-4892-b8ca-b0c903d5484c)
3. A failed download can leave a fake room.py that runs 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>The skill’s download loop redirects the gh api fallback into $f without checking whether it
>succeeds, while the scheduled watchdog prompt invokes python3 room.py watchdog without first
>verifying the download. When both download methods fail, room.py can be empty or contain an error
>body that Python treats as a no-op expression, so the watchdog never executes; the loop does not
>identify the failed file, and disabled task notifications leave the missing stall alarm unnoticed.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md[R37-40]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9/files#diff-7dcc95710d2eec6664574786a9d01b92d94822f644704261707e8c99202d7d73R37-R40) > >```diff >+for f in room.py "$DOC"; do >+ curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/$V/$f" -o "$f" || >+ gh api "repos/SigorMatt/agent-room/contents/$f?ref=$V" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" > "$f" >+done >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>SKILL.md[37-40] contains the fallback redirection but no per-file failure marker, unlike LEAD.md’s
>Setup, which prints FAILED $f; SKILL.md line 43 says to retry if both methods fail without giving
>the agent a clear signal that they did. ARCHITECT.md[196-206] places the download and `python3
>room.py watchdog` invocation on separate lines with no success check between them and disables
>scheduled-task notifications, while the alarm logic runs only if cmd_watchdog is invoked.
>
> > [.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md\[34-43\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md/#L34-L43) > [LEAD.md\[17-26\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/LEAD.md/#L17-L26) > [ARCHITECT.md\[190-205\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/ARCHITECT.md/#L190-L205) > [room.py\[2961-2977\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/room.py/#L2961-L2977) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The download instructions can leave `room.py` empty or containing a `gh api` error body after both download methods fail, then proceed to run it without identifying the failed file. The scheduled watchdog can consequently exit without executing its alarm logic while task notifications are disabled. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- .claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md[37-40] >- ARCHITECT.md[196-206] > >## Recommended Fix >Download the fallback output to a temporary file and move it into place only if `gh api` succeeds and the file is nonempty. On failure, remove the target, print `FAILED $f`, and stop the task with a nonzero status and a visible notification rather than invoking the watchdog. Before proceeding after a successful download, verify that `room.py` actually runs, for example with `python3 room.py --help >/dev/null`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/09f28bea-4337-4494-8041-d008537daede?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/09f28bea-4337-4494-8041-d008537daede)

4. Copied version line breaks the download URLs 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The architect's version lookup runs grep '^pipeline:', which prints the whole line (`pipeline:
>v1.0.0). The next step sets V=<version> without saying to strip the pipeline:` prefix, which
>room.py itself removes with ^pipeline:[ \t]*(\S+). If the line is used as is, both download URLs
>point at a nonexistent ref and the protocol won't load.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md[23]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/9/files#diff-7dcc95710d2eec6664574786a9d01b92d94822f644704261707e8c99202d7d73R23-R23) > >```diff >+ gh api "repos/OWNER/NAME/contents/docs/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md?ref=agent-room/state" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" | grep '^pipeline:' >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>room.py's playbook parser extracts only the token after pipeline:, while the skill's command
>returns the full line and then uses it as $V in raw.githubusercontent.com URLs.
>
> > [.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md\[21-35\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/.claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md/#L21-L35) > [room.py\[3014-3021\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/ea8170ab0d5c3b3e66fe3e5500e13b6918ed4b37/room.py/#L3014-L3021) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The skill's `grep '^pipeline:'` returns `pipeline: v1.0.0`, but `V` must be `v1.0.0` alone. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- .claude/skills/agent-room/SKILL.md[22-24] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace the grep with `sed -n 's/^pipeline:[[:space:]]*\([^[:space:]]*\).*/\1/p'` (or `awk '/^pipeline:/{print $2}'`) so the command prints only the version, matching room.py's own parse. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/ed3229ed-0d78-4b74-b632-494836d9e045?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/ed3229ed-0d78-4b74-b632-494836d9e045)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
